title: Profiles
goal: Pick the profile the interview is for and open its requirements.
primaryQuestion: Which profile am I interviewing for?
_why: The primary entry point of the app: an interviewer arrives with a position in mind, not with a wish to browse disciplines. Discipline is a global scope switched in the page actions; the tiles are destinations, which is what makes this a hub rather than a list.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: Name the screen for the chosen discipline. The discipline switch (SegmentedControl, .NET | Java) sits in the page actions on every screen, because discipline is the global scope, not a navigation level.

zones.name: tiles
zones.answers: Which profile am I interviewing for?
zones.purpose: One tile per profile of the current discipline: the profile name as the tile's link, a one-line placeholder descriptor, and four MetaItem counters in the tile's meta row saying how many skills are mandatory at Junior, Middle, Senior and Lead — the tile already shows that requirements differ by level, which is what the matrix inside will prove.

states.empty: EmptyState via the template's empty prop, reason no-data, icon=folder: the chosen discipline has no profiles yet; the action switches to the discipline that has some.
states.error: Static seed data cannot fail to load; a broken deep link resolves to the profiles of the current discipline, and the no-data case is the same EmptyState the empty state names.

data: profiles of the current discipline: name, descriptor (placeholder naming its field), mandatory-skill counts per seniority level — derived from the requirements, not stored

behaviours.given: profiles existing in several disciplines, one discipline chosen globally
behaviours.then: only the chosen discipline's profiles appear — the global scope IS the list
behaviours.why: The discipline switch is the app's one global control; a list that ignored it would fork the scope.
